web-search.description: Searches the web using DuckDuckGo and returns results (title, URL, snippet) as JSON. Use this when you need to find information about a topic you don't know, or when you need the latest information.
web-search.command: python3 -c "from ddgs import DDGS; import json,sys; print(json.dumps(DDGS().text('{{query}}', max_results=5), ensure_ascii=False))"

web-fetch.description: Fetches the content of a URL and returns it in Markdown format. Use this to read the full content of a page found via web-search.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from.

web-news.description: Searches recent news using DuckDuckGo and returns results as JSON. Use this when you specifically need the latest news about a topic.
web-news.command: python3 -c "from ddgs import DDGS; import json,sys; print(json.dumps(DDGS().news('{{query}}', max_results=5), ensure_ascii=False))"

read-image.description: Reads an image file and sends it to the mmproj-enabled LLM currently loaded on the llama.cpp server for analysis (thinking is disabled via chat_template_kwargs, so the model answers directly and briefly). Returns the model's description/answer about the image content. How to ask: phrase questions NEUTRALLY — ask the model to describe what is visible ('Describe the dog's pose'), not leading binary-choice options ('squatting or leg raised?'), because the offered option biases the answer (binary-choice bias observed empirically). Ask one fact per question and request one short sentence per item.

path.description: Absolute path to the image file (png, jpg, jpeg, bmp, webp).

prompt.description: Question or instruction about the image. Phrase it neutrally (describe what is visible), avoid binary-choice options; one fact per question, one short sentence per item (e.g., 'Describe the dog's pose').

danbooru-tags.description: Analyzes Danbooru (danbooru.donmai.us) posts.json for a given tag and reports which tags co-occur in real posts. It fetches SFW posts only (rating=safe), ranked by score (order=score), and prints a Markdown report: a Summary (population, sampling mode, distinct-tag counts per category), ranked tables of co-occurring General / Character / Copyright / Meta tags with frequency, and an optional verification section for candidate tags (verdict ADOPT / MODERATE / RARE / ABSENT per candidate). Use this to confirm whether a Danbooru tag actually exists and what vocabulary surrounds a character/work tag, when building an accurate anime image-generation prompt (it is a reliable substitute for the flaky tags/<name>.json show endpoint). How to interpret the output: (1) ADOPT identity tags with high frequency — character-specific appearance/costume tags (e.g. a forehead jewel, hair tubes, eye-of-horus for Ishizu Ishtar) anchor the character reliably. (2) Be judgmental about high-frequency body/revealing tags (breasts, cleavage, skirt_lift, ...): because sampling favors the most-rated SFW fanart, they may not fit the outfit/pose you are targeting — include only if it matches your intended design. (3) Ignore artist and meta tags — they should not appear in a character prompt. (4) If the report warns about a small sample (<10 posts) or reports 'sample of top-N', treat the frequencies as low-confidence. Caveats: SFW posts only (R18 analysis is out of scope); `tag` must be a single canonical Danbooru tag — underscore form preferred (space-form multi-word tags are auto-normalized to underscores); if the tag does not exist the report states TAG NOT FOUND explicitly. It also supports a sampling-independent tag-existence check: pass comma-separated exact tag names to `check` (use an empty `tag` and `limit` for a check-only run; `limit`/`verify` are ignored then). Each name is probed via posts.json?tags=<name>&limit=1 and reported as EXISTS (the name is a real canonical tag carried by posts), ALIAS (the name resolves to real posts but the posts use a different canonical name; candidate canonical names are listed), or NOT FOUND (no posts match the name; it most likely does not exist — express it in natural language or try a variant). Use `check` to settle exact spellings and catch invented tags: unlike `verify` (which measures co-occurrence inside a sampled SFW post set and can read ABSENT for real NSFW-centric tags such as ahegao/masturbation/pussy_juice), `check` is dictionary-level and sampling-independent.

tag.description: The single Danbooru tag to analyze (a character tag like 'ishizu_ishtar', a work tag like 'yu-gi-oh!', or a general tag). Underscore form is preferred; space-form multi-word tags are auto-normalized to underscores. Do not pass multiple tags. Pass an empty string when you only want the tag-existence check via `check`.

limit.description: Number of SFW posts to sample, 1-200 (Danbooru caps at 200). 50 is a good default for a balance of coverage and speed; 200 gives the fullest census for popular tags. Ignored in check-only runs (empty `tag`).

verify.description: Comma-separated list of candidate tags whose exact usage you want to verify (each is resolved against the sampled posts and given an ADOPT/MODERATE/RARE/ABSENT verdict; space-form names are auto-normalized). Pass an empty string if you do not need the verification section.

check.description: Comma-separated list of exact tag names to existence-check (each is probed dictionary-level via posts.json and given an EXISTS/ALIAS/NOT FOUND verdict; space-form names are auto-normalized). Use an empty `tag` for a check-only run. Pass an empty string if you do not need the existence-check section.

pdf-extract.description: Extracts text from a PDF file (pypdf-based). For PDFs web-fetch cannot parse (trafilatura returns no content for PDFs). Accepts a local absolute path OR an http(s) URL — URLs are downloaded once into %TEMP%/eca-pdf and cached, so research agents can read a paper PDF directly from a search result. Three output modes: mode=lines with a regex pattern returns matching lines with page markers and context; mode=text returns the extracted text with page markers (use to read a whole short paper); mode=raw returns text without markers. Defaults: pattern empty + mode=text reads the whole document; pattern given + mode=lines (default mode) searches; max_matches default 60 (cap 500); context_chars default 240 (40-2000). At most 400 pages are read. Errors are explicit: 'not a PDF file' (the URL served HTML — typical of paywalled publishers blocking non-browser clients, or the link is an abstract page), 'PDF is encrypted' (needs --password via CLI), 'needs the cryptography package' (AES-encrypted), 'no extractable text ... needs OCR' (scanned image PDF), 'pypdf is not installed'. Matched text is returned verbatim with page numbers — quote from it without reformatting formulas. Spec: tools/pdf_extract.md; tests: tools/tests/test_pdf_extract.py.

path.description: Absolute path to the PDF file, or an http(s) URL of a PDF (downloaded and cached automatically).

pattern.description: Regex searched line by line, case-insensitive (e.g. 'surface tension|curvature'). Empty string = no search.

mode.description: lines (matching lines with page markers), text (whole document, page markers), or raw (whole document, no markers). Empty string = lines when a pattern is given, text otherwise.

max_matches.description: Maximum matches to report (default 60, cap 500). Ignored outside lines mode.

context_chars.description: Characters of context on each side of a match (default 240, range 40-2000). Ignored outside lines mode.

tagger.description: Tags anime images with danbooru tags using the local SmilingWolf/wd-eva02-large-tagger-v3 model (tools/tagger.py + tools/models/model.safetensors, CPU inference via torch/timm — this is a tag *classifier*, not a vision-language model: it cannot answer questions about an image, use read-image for that). Accepts one or more absolute image paths as SEPARATE space-separated tokens (jpg jpeg png bmp webp tga; a directory token expands to the images inside it, and overlapping tokens are de-duplicated) and runs them as one batch. Prefer plain file/directory tokens; use a glob token only when nothing else is passed, because the script resolves glob tokens relative to the current directory, so mixing a glob with other tokens or pointing one at another drive can fail with NotImplementedError (Non-relative patterns are unsupported). Returns stdout JSON only: {"images": [{"file": "<path>", "tags": [{"tag": "1girl", "score": 0.98}, ...]}]} with tags sorted by score descending, scores rounded to 4 decimals, and rating/character/general merged into one flat list (rating tags general/sensitive/questionable/explicit are always present in the output; for a real anime image the rating is general = safe). Typical anime photos yield roughly 10-40 tags above 0.35. All three arguments are required: use threshold 0.35 and limit 20 as the typical values (raise threshold for a short high-confidence list, lower it for a fuller vocabulary dump; limit 0 = unlimited). Model/CSV paths are resolved inside the script (TAGGER_MODEL/TAGGER_TAGS -> tools/models/), so they are not exposed here. Errors are returned with a non-zero exit and a JSON message {"error": ..., "details": ...} on stderr (common ones: 対象の画像が見つかりませんでした = the paths matched nothing, 一部の画像ファイルが存在しません = a typo'd or missing path, モデルファイルが見つかりません / tag 一覧 CSV が見つかりません = tools/models/ files missing, モデル出力サイズと tag 一覧の行数が一致しません = model and selected_tags.csv are not a matching pair). Spec: tools/tagger.md; a single inference pass takes on the order of tens of seconds on CPU.

images.description: Absolute image file or directory paths as separate tokens joined by single spaces (e.g. 'C:/img/a.png C:/imgs C:/other/b.jpg'). A directory token expands to the images it contains, and tokens that overlap are de-duplicated. Do NOT wrap the whole list in one pair of quotes and do not use paths containing spaces — a single quoted multi-path string reaches the script as one argument. Glob tokens (* ? [) are resolved against the current working directory, so pass a glob only on its own; mixing a glob with plain tokens or pointing one at a different drive can raise NotImplementedError (Non-relative patterns are unsupported). An empty value returns the error 対象の画像が見つかりませんでした with no output; a non-existent plain path returns 一部の画像ファイルが存在しません with details.missing.

threshold.description: Minimum tag score to report, 0-1. Required; use 0.35 as the typical value (the script's own default) — it yields a usable tag list for most anime images. Raise it (0.5-0.7) for a short high-confidence list, lower it (0.1-0.25) for a fuller vocabulary dump.

limit.description: Max tags returned per image. Required; use 20 as the typical value (the script's own default). 0 = unlimited (returns every tag above threshold), 10 caps to the most confident tags only.
